findings.failure_path: stop_notice keys the marker on module.actor(payload) and module.regular_info(path). That path comes from agent_transcript_path when the payload has one, but extraction_overflow and proposed_next scan transcript_path. If a subagent payload carries both and the scanned transcript_path is replaced, the marker still uses the unchanged agent transcript's inode, so the new transcript gets no fresh notice. This breaks acceptance item 3. No test sends agent_transcript_path.
findings.smallest_fix: Build the claim epoch from os.fstat of the transcript_path that was actually scanned, or compare the agent path with transcript_path and skip deduplication when they differ. Add a subprocess test with agent_transcript_path set and transcript_path replaced.

concern_results.conclusion: Checked all four areas in the diff. Optional helper: stop_notice catches Exception, so a missing, raising or unparseable skill-loading.py still produces the notice, and the tests cover all three cases. Native invocation: extraction_overflow uses the current context's requested_skills, so a pending or failed Claude Skill request still counts. Codex only counts after a complete successful read. Evidence completeness: context_transcript returns unknown for incomplete context, and proposed_next re-raises when nothing makes the session eligible. Checks are never skipped: markers are consulted only after the check, and only to decide whether to print the notice. One flaw: the notice identity can be tied to the wrong transcript (see finding).

Actor and marker inputs can only hide the advisory notice. They cannot turn a missing check into a block or a pass. The whole-session transcript command stays strict. Unsafe state (the symlinked state directory) falls back to printing the notice, and the test confirms nothing is written to the symlink target. The overflow path never blocks the extraction gate, so it cannot bypass one. H9 and H10 (package and release checks) are still pending, and the plan says so.
